status: Internally specified after the PMLB and NIPS analyses but before selecting columns or scoring any UCI HAR model; no public registration.
source: Reyes-Ortiz and colleagues, UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones, DOI 10.24432/C54S4K, CC BY 4.0. Use the original supplier's 561 engineered columns and official 21-person train / nine-person test split.
question: On the official held-out participants, how does the transferred separating selector compare to Gain and recursive feature elimination at the identical retained width, and to selectors with independently fixed budgets?
partition: Use sklearn GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1,test_size=0.25,random_state=20421) within the official training subjects for inner fitting/ranking. Never split windows of one person between fitting and ranking. The nine official test subjects enter only after all supports and fitted predictions are frozen. Test activity labels are read only by the separate outcome scorer.
predictor: Unmodified PMLB CPU XGBClassifier, 100 boosting rounds, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.1, histogram splits, n_jobs=1, random_state=20421. No learned transformation on supplied finite engineered columns. All final refits use the same full official training rows. Source-supplied engineered feature transformations are taken as given.
voting: Original direct block/singleton search and unchanged geometry, anchor, four panels and tolerances. Use the PMLB 20421 seed for training and panel sampling. Nested, separating and three equal-size/count independent random designs with seeds 77531, 100000, 200000. The random designs share panels and anchor; they are not independent test cohorts.
controls: Full; independently sized compact Gain; Gain prefix donating the separating width on the same inner-training ranking; native sklearn RFE with XGB gain, step=0.20, on all official training people at the separating width; prespecified native RFE and XGB Gain prefixes on all official training people at externally supplied budgets 1%, 10%, 25%, 50% (ceil of 561 times fraction, unused columns ordered last by index). Every support evaluated regardless of outcome.
primary: Mean of nine within-person window accuracies, equal participant weights. Report separating minus width-matched RFE and width-matched Gain together, all nine paired differences, their median and range. Cohort descriptive analysis, no formal population noninferiority or significance claims.
secondary: Pooled accuracy, macro one-vs-rest AUC on all official test windows, proportion of engineered features retained, actual unique masks, charged selection and final refit/prediction seconds. Fixed budgets and supplied-width controls are labeled. One cohort, one model seed, no test-informed tuning, no uncited sensor-cost claims.
cost: Measure each selector under one XGBoost thread and separately measure each final refit/prediction, even when supports coincide. Cache common reference fit and anchor only within an arm; run every route independently from data resident in memory. Donor-width times exclude the cost of obtaining k and are conditional. Record the actual native RFE cost including its internal final fit and the common subsequent refit. Worker cutoff 3600 seconds for the entire dataset/run, with persistent stage logs. Keep all failed attempts.
label_access: Acquisition copies the public binary zip. Archive listing/byte hashing do not parse test outcomes. Freeze all feature sets, model/split settings, and test-set predictions before parsing y_test.txt. A separate scoring pass validates code, protocol, data, supports and prediction hashes.
